# Hexagonal hardening model and consumer inventory

Pin: 8a961000859c02862454338fda6c4dd65bda2aa1

Commit: Add a hermetic, versioned JSON export of the build graph with
unrendered recipes (#858) (#923)

Date: 2026-10-23

Toolchain: `nightly-2026-10-22`

This document is a dated snapshot owned by RFC 0026. Every `path:line` citation
is valid only at the declared pin. RFC 0027 owns automated coverage. The
register records evidence; it is not proof. The API-negative and compile-fail
tests in task 26.2.1 remain the backstop.

## Scope and definitions

The seven areas follow RFC 0026's compiler and execution boundaries:

- **A1 — Authored model and loading:** manifest types in `src/ast/`, their
  deserializers and conversions, manifest loaders, environment processing,
  in-place Jinja rendering, and the conditional-target filter used by help.
- **A2 — Lowering:** `BuildGraph::from_manifest*`, rule and target processing,
  recipe resolution, action registration, output insertion, and command
  interpolation bindings.
- **A3 — Graph storage:** `BuildGraph`, `Action`, `BuildEdge`, `EdgeId`, the IR
  dependency order, and `ActionHasher`.
- **A4 — Backend consumers:** Ninja and dyndep generation, command-list
  rendering, shell quoting and escaping, graph projections, graph JSON export,
  and the `lint`-feature rules that inspect recipes or follow rule delegation.
- **A5 — CLI orchestration:** command/configuration values, runner dispatch,
  manifest-to-graph generation, shell selection, Ninja invocation, and
  command-facing entry points.
- **A6 — Diagnostics:** IR, Ninja, manifest, and runner errors; localization;
  diagnostic and success JSON; and process exit-code rendering.
- **A7 — Existing seams:** process requests and environment, status reporting,
  clock parameters, capability-scoped directories, temporary-file and dyndep
  leases, and their test substitutes.

**Production** means code compiled into the library, binary, or `build.rs`
without `cfg(test)` or `cfg(kani)`, for the host and all features. Tests,
doctests, benches, `test_support`, inline test modules, and Kani-only code are
listed in the appendix because later changes must migrate them too.

A **constructor** creates an inventoried value through a literal, variant,
tuple constructor, `Self` variant, `Default`, conversion, or deserializer. A
**mutator** changes an existing value through a mutable receiver or parameter,
field write, collection operation, or `mem::{take, replace, swap}`. A
**consumer** reads fields, matches variants, or calls query methods. A
**visibility class** is `pub`, `pub` with `#[doc(hidden)]`, crate-internal
(`pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, or `pub(in ..)`), or private. **API-reachable**
marks a public or doc-hidden constructor or mutator whether or not in-tree
production code calls it.

Each location is valid only at the declared pin. A site identifier names the
area, inventoried item, enclosing module-qualified symbol, and site kind. When
multiple uses of one item occur in the same enclosing symbol, the row lists all
their line anchors. The oracle can warn more than once for one expression when
it uses several annotated fields or variants; those item-specific records are
retained separately.

## Method

The oracle used an archive of the approved pin under the ignored
`target/inventory-26-1-1/` directory. `annotate_oracle.py` added 561
`#[deprecated(note = "inventory")]` markers in 61 files: selected type and
field declarations, enum variants, inherent methods, named free functions,
constants, and `EdgeId` itself. It did not annotate trait implementation blocks
or trait methods; rustc rejects those annotations under `useless_deprecated`,
and dispatch through `Default`, `From`, `Deserialize`, and related traits is
covered by the text sweep.

The single host build command was:

```sh
CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$SCRATCH/target" \
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --message-format=json
```

It passed on 2026-10-25 with 11,197 compiler warning messages. Deduplicating
primary spans by `file:line:column` and warning message produced 7,881 primary
sites. The line-based context normalizer produced 3,062 unique production
records and 4,761 test-only records. Twenty-eight records occur in both build
contexts, in `src/host/pattern.rs` and `src/localization/mod.rs`. These are
different measures: primary spans retain column identity, while context records
retain the resolved symbol and source line. The following warning-message
totals group fields and variants under their parent and combine same-named
helper functions; their sum is the compiler message count.

Three corrected text sweeps cover compiler blind spots. The Rust source list
contains 936 files across `src/`, `build.rs`, `tests/`, `test_support/`,
`benches/`, and the two-file `build_slice_fixture` compile contract. The
constructor and mutation pattern produced 2,486 raw candidate lines. The
trait-dispatch pattern produced 897 exact candidate lines after adding
`CommandIsolation` to the type set; the earlier 942-line count included the
broader exploratory `::new` expansion and is superseded. The doctest-comment
pattern produced 159 candidates: 119 under `src/`, 18 under `tests/`, 10 under
`test_support/`, and 12 additional `CommandIsolation` references. Raw matches
are candidates, not sites. The targeted classifier checked the candidates
against pinned source and the compiler records. It added the trait conversion at
`src/ir/from_manifest/mod.rs:168` and identified two Kani-only variant uses:
`DependencyOrder::Parallel` at `src/ir/cycle/verification.rs:346` and
`StringOrList::Empty` at `src/ir/from_manifest/verification.rs:38`. The
separate unit-variant sweep had 247 raw matches, with the remaining candidates
in tests, examples, and comments. The unregistered production set was empty
once compiler warnings, trait-dispatch constructors, and cfg-only candidates
were reconciled. Test, doctest, bench, support, and Kani contexts are listed in
the appendix.

The candidate patterns were:

```text
T = Action|BuildEdge|BuildGraph|EdgeId|Recipe|RawRecipe|Rule|Target|
    NetsukeManifest|StringOrList|DependencyOrder|CommandIsolation
P = \b(Self|T)(::\w+)?\s*[{(] | &mut\s+T\b
  | mem::(take|replace|swap) | &mut self | \bmut self\b
  | self\s*:\s*&mut
  | \.(retain|clear|insert|push|extend|values_mut|iter_mut)\(
Trait = \b(T)::default\( | Default::default | \.into\(\)
      | from_(str|value|slice|reader)\b
Doctest = ^\s*//[/!] .*\b(T)\b
```

`T` includes `CommandIsolation` in the corrected follow-up. The first pattern
was run over every file in the source list; the trait pattern covered
trait-dispatched construction, and the comment pattern selected doctest
candidates for file-only review.

**EV-REVERSE (2026-10-25).** All 1,748 unique register rows were checked at the
pin. Their 3,009 explicit `path:line` anchors all resolve to existing files and
in-range lines; the 69 type-table anchors match the declared type or constant.
The site rows are sourced from resolved compiler warning locations, with the
trait-dispatch and API-reachable rows checked against their implementations and
call sites. A fictitious `BuildGraph::remove_edge` row had no match in
`src/ir/graph/mod.rs`.

The test-module pass found 293 `cfg(test|kani)` markers, 138 explicit test/Kani
module declarations, 5 path-included modules, 224 test-only external
modules/files, 4 Kani external files, and 57 inline test modules.

The annotated scratch build marked 561 declarations, fields, variants,
constants, and functions in 61 files. It did not annotate trait implementation
blocks or trait methods, which `rustc` rejects with `useless_deprecated`; the
trait sweep covers those dispatch paths. The scratch-only source tree and build
target were removed after collecting the records. The inventory retains only
the resulting pin-specific evidence.

**EV-SEEDED (2026-10-25).** A separate pinned export tested P1–P12 without
showing the classifier their locations. The compiler and sweep found P1–P6 and
P10; the sweep found P7, P8, P11, and P12 in the expected non-host or Kani
regions; P9's 12 compiler sites and 2 sweep lines were classified test-only.
All 11 production/Kani controls were found, the test control was classified
correctly, and there were no misses. The seeded build recorded 7,877 primary
sites before and 7,912 after seeding. That experiment used the then-current
934-file sweep; the corrected follow-up added two `build_slice_fixture` files
and `CommandIsolation` to the candidate type set. The follow-up found no new
constructor/mutator lines in the fixture and added three exact trait-pattern
candidates. The primary oracle was then rerun after adding the omitted
`MISSING_RECIPE_ERROR` marker; this accounts for the current 7,881-site and
11,197-warning baseline. The first seeded build failed only on seven
missing-doc errors in scratch helpers; they were documented and the second
build passed without lint suppression.

#### CLI field classification

`Cli` fields read by runner and merge code fall into two groups. Semantic or
execution inputs are `file`, `directory`, `config`, `jobs`, all fetch and
environment allow/block fields, `fetch_default_deny`,
`trust_project_fetch_policy`, the seven manifest budgets,
`interaction.no_input`, `default_targets`, and `command`. Presentation fields
are `verbose`, `locale`, `json`, `color`, `emoji`, `progress`, and
`accessibility`. The site rows above retain the exact readers; `json` is
presentation data that currently also selects child stderr routing (OBS-15).

## Landed work

These changes predate the pin. Their contracts remain in force; this inventory
schedules no repeat of issue `#652`.

- `#652` / PR `#714` (`2c030fd1`) moved graph edges into a canonical edge
  arena. Preserve alias identity, atomic duplicate rejection, and no per-output
  cloning (CO-14).
- `#705` closed the typed redirect boundary work and completed the H6 context;
  retain its redirect-policy limits when assessing later acquisition work.
- `#699` and ADR-0027 established the command-placeholder contract. Preserve
  placeholder substitution and shell quoting (CO-7).
- `#753` and ADR-0034 preserved script `in` and `out` values as shell
  variables, with the ADR's shell-level behaviour retained (CO-7).
- `#754` added the JSON excerpt guard; preserve excerpt redaction and bounds
  (CO-5).
- `#696` introduced the injected monotonic-clock seam. Keep clock ownership
  injectable in generation and status flows (CO-10).
- `#811` regrouped prefix-named modules into directory modules. All register
  anchors use the post-regrouping paths at this pin.
- `#857` and ADR-0045 added isolated command-list entries. Preserve their
  separate rendering and validation across interpreters (CO-15).
- ADR-0041 established the canonical `shell_quote` and `shell_join` surface;
  keep shell quoting separate from Ninja escaping (CO-7).
- `#778` added manifest-facing shell-selection vocabulary under
  `src/shell_selection/`; it is not yet wired into authored types or lowering
  and remains distinct from `RecipeShell` under ADR-0044.
- `#858` and ADR-0044 added the graph JSON export. Preserve its schema and
  semantics as a committed external surface (CO-4).
- `#592` and ADR-0056 added `netsuke check`. Its rules are compiler consumers
  and must migrate with graph and recipe semantics.
- The pin is 79 commits after the planning baseline `ebcedaef`; 45 intervening
  commits touched in-scope paths. The earlier RFC 0026 audit also predates 113
  commits, 17 of which touched `src/`. The current register replaces that
  earlier file-level snapshot rather than copying its observations.

## Findings

The findings below describe the pinned implementation. They are observations,
not decisions to change policy. Each has an owning roadmap task.

- H1: `Action.recipe` stores authored `ast::Recipe` in
  `src/ir/graph/mod.rs:252-269`; its production constructor is
  `register_action` in `src/ir/from_manifest/support/mod.rs:47-60`. `BuildEdge`
  has public fields and is constructed in `process_targets` at
  `src/ir/from_manifest/mod.rs:164-174`. `BuildGraph` derives `Default` and
  exposes `actions` and `default_targets`. `insert_edge` checks output alias
  collisions but not that `action_id` exists; the public
  `replace_edge_for_output` can replace an edge while retaining aliases. These
  facts leave invalid graph states constructible (26.2.1, 26.2.2, 26.2.3).
- H2: Neither `BuildGraph` nor `Action` retains the interpreter. The
  doc-hidden `BuildGraph::from_manifest_for_shell` and
  `ninja_gen::generate_with_shell` accept it independently; default generation
  and dyndep paths choose `RecipeShell::host_default()`. The build and generate
  runner paths thread the selected shell and optional Bash executable through
  both stages; graph, help-targets, and check paths lower with the host default
  (26.3.1, 26.3.2).
- H3: `runner::execute_build` and `runner::execute_ninja_tool` interleave
  generation, dyndep publication, temporary-manifest creation, and Ninja spawn
  while reading `Cli`. `NinjaBuildRequest` and `NinjaToolRequest` do not contain
  `Cli`; `StderrMode::from_json_enabled(cli.json)` still uses a presentation
  field for child-stream routing, and `open_effective_dir(cli)` re-derives
  directory authority from `cli.directory` (27.2.1, 27.2.2, 27.2.3).
- H4: `IrGenError` pairs structured facts with `LocalizedMessage` in several
  variants and uses a static string in `InvalidManifest`. `NinjaGenError` mixes
  localized variants with fixed-English `#[error]` variants. Neither enum is
  `#[non_exhaustive]` or carries a `miette` code; JSON therefore emits null for
  their codes. `localize_recipe_error` classifies three validation failures with
  `starts_with` checks (27.1.1, 27.1.2, 27.1.3).

Observed details and ownership:

- OBS-1: a rule whose recipe is `rule: other` passes lowering and validation;
  `NamedAction::reject_rule_recipe` panics in debug builds and returns
  `UnsafeNinjaValue` in release builds. Existing linter tests cover one-hop
  delegation and a delegation cycle (26.1.2, 26.2.2).
- OBS-2: duplicate rule names are last-wins in `process_rules`
  (`src/ir/from_manifest/mod.rs:98-102`) (26.1.2).
- OBS-3: `DuplicateOutput` is built with two argument shapes in graph storage
  and lowering (`src/ir/graph/mod.rs:65-70`,
  `src/ir/from_manifest/support/mod.rs:158-173`) (27.1.1).
- OBS-4: `MissingAction` is built in both normal and dyndep generation
  (`src/ninja_gen/mod.rs:185-189`, `src/ninja_gen/dyndep/mod.rs:195-199`)
  (27.1.1).
- OBS-5: `localize_recipe_error` classifies three recipe failures by string
  prefix (`src/manifest/registration.rs:118-136`) (27.1.2).
- OBS-6: IR and Ninja errors have no diagnostic code (27.1.3).
- OBS-7: `generate_with_shell` and the host-default `generate*` and
  `generate_bundle` paths accept an unchecked interpreter (26.3.1).
- OBS-8: graph, help-targets, and check lower with the host-default
  interpreter, unlike build and generate (26.3.1). OBS-9 is withdrawn; it was
  incorrect at its first review and is not a finding.
- OBS-10: public fields, `Default`, `insert_edge`, and
  `replace_edge_for_output` can create dangling or swapped `action_id` values
  (`src/ir/graph/mod.rs:39-48,62-72,161-175`) (26.2.1).
- OBS-11: `assert_shell_command` panics only in debug builds and is also called
  by command-list rendering (`src/ninja_gen/mod.rs:247-254`,
  `src/ninja_gen/command_list/render.rs`) (26.2.2).
- OBS-12: manifest rendering mutates authored types in place, including the
  `rule:` selector, in build and manifest-query modes
  (`src/manifest/render/mod.rs`) (26.1.2, 26.2.1).
- OBS-13: the Kani `insert_edge` implementation returns `EdgeId` unconditionally
  (`src/ir/graph/mod.rs:75-78`) (26.2.3).
- OBS-14: all four error enums are exhaustive and publicly constructible
  (27.1.1).
- OBS-15: `StderrMode` follows `cli.json` (27.2.1).
- OBS-16: `open_effective_dir` re-derives directory authority per call
  (27.2.2).
- OBS-17: graph JSON maps every empty command recipe to `dependency_only`,
  regardless of isolation, unlike `Recipe::is_dependency_only`
  (`src/runner/help/graph_json.rs:206-235`) (26.2.1).
- OBS-18: linter rules follow `Recipe::Rule` delegation through
  `manifest.rules`, creating a second consumer of delegation semantics
  (`src/lint/rules/{graph,caching,hygiene}/mod.rs`) (26.2.2).
- OBS-19: `#592` landed and `docs/netsuke-linter-design.md` records that the
  linter reconstructs source origins heuristically because `NetsukeManifest`
  retains none. This is an entry-condition fact for 27.3.1; this inventory does
  not decide whether that conditional work proceeds.

## Compatibility obligations

- CO-1: Preserve manifest acceptance and rejection, including the missing
  recipe, empty command-list, command-isolation, and mutual-exclusion messages.
  Evidence: manifest parser, deserializer, and recipe-validation tests. Tasks:
  26.1.2, 26.2.1, 26.2.2, 27.1.2.
- CO-2: Preserve generated Ninja bytes and repeated-run determinism through
  both normal emission and dyndep, including isolated command-list entries.
  Evidence: Ninja snapshots and command-list integration tests. Tasks: 26.2.2,
  26.2.3, 26.3.1, 26.3.2.
- CO-3: Preserve action identity. `ActionHasher::hash` hashes the RFC 8785

### Excluded

None. Every task in the 26.1.1 dependency closure has a Changes or Consumes row
above. Conditional 27.3 work is outside that closure and has no dependency on
this inventory at the pin.

### Unchanged

None as a whole register area. Every register item is either named in a change
row or retained as context by the inventory-consuming policy and evaluation
rows above. These references do not authorize a source change by this task.

## Consuming this inventory

A consuming ExecPlan cites the relevant register identifiers in its
`Conformance basis`, then inspects changes since the pin before relying on any
site: `git log <pin>..HEAD -- src build.rs tests test_support benches`. It
re-sweeps each in-scope file changed since the pin and records its new line
anchors in that consumer's own evidence. The inventory stays a historical
snapshot.

## Refreshing this inventory

A refresh produces a new pin and revises the whole document against that tree.
It keeps existing register identifiers stable, adds new identifiers as needed,
and never reuses retired identifiers. Consumers continue to cite the pin they
actually reviewed.
